questions.question: Users search an HR index for "cab reimbursement", but the policy text says "taxi fares are refunded". Keyword queries return no results. What should you add first?

options.text: A filter on the department field
options.why: Filters narrow results. They do not add synonyms.

options.text: A vector query that uses an embedding of the question
options.why: Correct. Vector search matches meaning, so related wording is found.

options.text: A larger top value on the keyword query
options.why: A larger result count does not match words that do not appear.

options.text: A scoring profile that boosts the title field
options.why: Boosting reorders matches. It cannot create matches for words that are absent.

questions.explanation: Keyword search matches tokens. Vector search finds semantically similar text.

questions.question: A hybrid query returns results with scores such as 0.0328 and 0.0164. What explains the small values?

options.text: The query exceeded the service's query rate limit
options.why: Throttling returns an error. It does not alter scores.

options.text: The results are merged and scored by using Reciprocal Rank Fusion
options.why: Correct. RRF scores are sums of reciprocal ranks, so they are small and unrelated to BM25 or similarity values.

options.text: The semantic ranker returned scores on a 0 to 4 scale
options.why: Reranker scores are reported on a 0 to 4 scale, and these values are not.

options.text: The vector index uses scalar quantization
options.why: Quantization affects storage and recall, not the scale of fused scores.

questions.explanation: Hybrid queries merge keyword and vector lists with RRF.

questions.question: A query that uses queryType semantic fails because the index has no semantic configuration. Which statement about the semantic ranker is correct?

options.text: It reranks at most the top 50 results of the first-stage query and needs a semantic configuration on the index
options.why: Correct. It is a second-stage reranker that reads the fields named in the configuration.

options.text: It replaces the vectorizer, so no embedding model is needed
options.why: It does not create embeddings. Vector queries still need them.

options.text: It retrieves documents that the keyword and vector queries did not return
options.why: The ranker only reorders results that the first stage returned.

options.text: It runs on the whole index before the keyword query
options.why: It is applied after the first-stage query, to the top results only.

questions.explanation: The semantic ranker is a second-stage reranker over the top 50.

questions.question: A support index must find exact error codes such as E-1074 and also match natural language descriptions. Vector-only queries return unrelated articles for codes. Which query type should you use?

options.text: Hybrid, with a keyword query and a vector query in one request
options.why: Correct. Keyword matching keeps exact codes and vectors cover the descriptions.

options.text: Keyword only, with a synonym map for every code
options.why: This does not cover free-form descriptions and is hard to maintain.

options.text: Vector only, with a larger k
options.why: A larger k returns more neighbours but does not make codes match exactly.

options.text: Semantic ranker only, with no first-stage query
options.why: The ranker needs first-stage results to reorder.

questions.explanation: Hybrid search combines exact matching and meaning matching.

questions.question: Documents were embedded with text-embedding-3-small. Which two statements about querying the vector field are correct?

options.text: Vector queries cannot be combined with keyword queries in one request
options.why: They can, and that combination is a hybrid query.

options.text: A vector query can include filters that are applied before or after the nearest-neighbour search
options.why: Correct. preFilter and postFilter modes control the order.

options.text: Any embedding model can be used for the query because all vectors are interchangeable
options.why: Vectors from different models live in different spaces and give poor results.

options.text: Query text must be embedded with the same model, which a vectorizer on the index can do
options.why: Correct. Vectors from different models are not comparable.

questions.explanation: The query and the documents must share an embedding model, and filters can be combined with vector queries.
